title: Canonical tail loop
statement: Let $A$ be a program with $m$ registers, control states in $\Lambda$, and oracle deciders indexed by $d$, and choose pairwise distinct registers $\mathsf{ptr},\mathsf{limit},\mathsf{cap}$. Suppose the loop compares the pointer with the limit, reads a decider answer at the binary encoding of the pointer value, halves the cap register, and advances the pointer by a fixed stride before repeating; on reaching the limit it reports done or fail according to a supplied final bit, while a zero cap or a failed length check leads to fail. Assume $\mathsf{stride}>0$ and the stated transitions of $A$ implement these branches, query, halving, and stride increments exactly. Let $w$ be a Boolean word, let $\mathit{last}$ be a Boolean bit, and suppose all initial registers are at most $B$, the limit equals the pointer plus $\mathsf{stride}\,|w|$, and each oracle query at pointer value plus $\mathsf{stride}\,i$ returns bit $i$ of $w$ for every $i<|w|$ (defaulting to false when absent). Then there are final register values, still bounded by $B$, with the pointer at most the limit and every register other than the pointer and cap unchanged, such that the program reaches the control state determined as follows: if $|w|$ is at most the bit length of the initial cap, it reports done when the last bit of $w$ (defaulting to $\mathit{last}$ for an empty word) is true, and fail otherwise; if the length exceeds that bit length, it reports fail. Every intervening configuration satisfies the program’s safety conditions and keeps all registers bounded by $B$.
